Subject: Proposed round-robin exec windows for tri-region demos

Hi Emma and Yuki —

Thanks again for the steady momentum on the POC. One scheduling wrinkle keeps popping up: our execs (and yours) span US / EU / APAC and we keep ending up asking the same people to attend at inconvenient hours. With the pipeline heating up, I want to propose a lightweight "round-robin" cadence for exec-level demo windows so we can:

- Distribute off-hour burden fairly across leaders
- Keep demo slots predictable for the customer stakeholders
- Avoid repeated last-minute reschedules when a single exec is blocked

High-level proposal (attached): round_robin_demo_plan.pdf — 4-week rotation with three anchor windows (one per region). Each week we present in the window that best matches the target region; if an exec is unavailable we fall back to the next compatible window. Also attaching a timezone_matrix.csv with candidate slot conversions.

Concrete asks: can you both share the primary execs who should be on the call (name + timezone + hard no windows), and indicate whether you can support two 60-min pilot demos next week in these anchor windows?

Anchor windows (local suggestion):
- US-friendly: 09:00–11:00 PST (roughly 17:00–19:00 CET / 01:00–03:00 JST)
- EU-friendly: 14:00–16:00 CET (roughly 05:00–07:00 PST / 22:00–00:00 JST)
- APAC-friendly: 10:00–12:00 JST (roughly 18:00–20:00 CET / 09:00–11:00 PST)

Notes: EU/US DST are settled this month, but there are edge-cases for multinational execs crossing travel dates in the coming quarter — the attached matrix flags daylight-savings-sensitive ranges.

I'll follow up with a concrete rotation table once we get primary exec constraints.

Thanks —
Rishi

Thanks Rishi — good call. A few quick clarifications from my side:

1) Please ask customer execs for their hard-no days (e.g., "no Mondays" or "only mornings CET"). We need that to avoid repeating the same failed attempts.
2) Instead of a strict 4-week rotation, can we pilot a 2-week rotation for the first month and measure attendee fatigue? If it's stable we expand to 4 weeks.
3) Suggestion on anchor windows: include a short overlap buffer of 15 minutes at the ends to allow handoffs between regional teams.

I did a quick pass on the timeline and propose two pilot slots next week (I converted to UTC below):
- Pilot A (EU-first week): 2026-11-24 14:00–15:00 CET (2026-11-24 13:00–14:00 UTC)
- Pilot B (US-first week): 2026-11-26 09:30–10:30 PST (2026-11-26 17:30–18:30 UTC)

If Emma/Yuki can confirm primary execs and hard-no windows by EOD Monday (23 Nov), I can lock the invites and add the rotation calendar objects.

—Lauren

Folks —

Thanks for the input. I took Rishi's anchor windows and Emma's constraints and put together a rotation matrix and sample UTC slots (attached timezone_matrix.csv and round_robin_demo_plan.pdf). Key points:

- Pilot plan: two pilot demos (24 Nov EU-first, 26 Nov US-first) as Lauren suggested.
- Rotation mechanics: 2-week pilot rotation (Week A: EU-anchor, Week B: US-anchor) with APAC-anchor as the weekend/alternate week slot. After the pilot we'll evaluate to move to 4-week rotation.
- Fallback policy: if primary exec is no-go we have an automated fallback to the next window and an optional recorded short executive briefing (15 minutes).
- Implementation: I created calendar objects (proposed_slots.ics) that encode the rotation with a 15-minute buffer; those are ready to drop into the invites once we lock exec availability.

Sample conversions (UTC):
- EU-anchor pilot (24 Nov): 13:00–14:00 UTC (14:00–15:00 CET, 05:00–06:00 PST, 22:00–23:00 JST)
- US-anchor pilot (26 Nov): 17:30–18:30 UTC (09:30–10:30 PST, 18:30–19:30 CET, 03:30–04:30 JST next day) — note the JST late-night edge.

Attachments in this message: round_robin_demo_plan.pdf (proposal with rotation table), timezone_matrix.csv (detailed conversions), proposed_slots.ics (calendar objects).

If Emma can confirm Sarah's hard no windows and Miguel's Fridays constraint by Monday, I'll publish the pilot invites and mark them with the HubSpot record (HubSpot:48019).
